hit.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
hit.body: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation model with stronger capabilities in coding, science, and cybersecurity, paired with its most advanced safety stack.
hit.reason: OpenAI's new model announcement requires review of the OpenAI-to-Bedrock migration guide to assess whether GPT-5.6 Sol changes the competitive positioning, pricing, or model mapping recommendations for migrations from OpenAI to AWS Bedrock.

step1.summary: GPT-5.6 Sol is a newly previewed OpenAI model with no pricing or benchmark data yet; the migration guide's model tables only go up to GPT-5.5 and don't reference it.
step1.old_value: Latest documented flagship is GPT-5.5 (April 23, 2026), $5.00/$30.00 per 1M tokens, with comparison tables against Bedrock models.
step1.new_value: GPT-5.6 Sol previewed as next-gen model (coding, science, cybersecurity, safety improvements); no pricing, context window, or availability details given in announcement.
step1.still_true: All existing GPT-5.5 and earlier pricing/comparison data remains valid until GPT-5.6 Sol pricing is announced.
step1.reasoning: This is a preview announcement with no pricing or technical specs, so it cannot yet update the pricing/comparison tables in ai-openai-to-bedrock.md; it should be tracked as new knowledge to watch for once pricing details emerge, since the file currently has no entry for GPT-5.6 Sol at all.

affected.after: ### GPT-5.5 Series (previous flagship — April 23, 2026; superseded by GPT-5.6 Sol preview)
affected.why: The heading claims GPT-5.5 is the 'Latest' model, but the announcement introduces GPT-5.6 Sol as the new next-generation model, making this labeling outdated.
affected.evidence_quote: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model

step2.notes: [b1] The announcement only previews GPT-5.6 Sol with no pricing, context window, or availability details, and explicitly states all existing GPT-5.5 and earlier pricing/comparison data remains valid until GPT-5.6 Sol pricing is announced. Therefore almost all GPT-5.5 pricing/comparison content in these files is unaffected — it should NOT be rewritten to reference GPT-5.6 Sol since there is no comparable data (price, context window) to substitute. The one genuinely affected line is the '(Latest — April 23, 2026)' heading, which asserts GPT-5.5 is the most recent/latest model — that claim is now stale since GPT-5.6 Sol has been previewed as the next-generation model. This is a 'value' type change (a label claiming latest status) rather than a full judgment reversal, since no comparison judgments about cost superiority are reversed (no pricing exists yet for GPT-5.6 Sol to compare).
